description: Static common-clock CPU4096 envelope audit; no workload/calibration executed.

timer.resolution_provenance: Query the native calibration executable; advertised resolution is distinct from consecutive-call deltas.

clang_version:
Homebrew clang version 22.1.8
Target: arm64-apple-darwin27.0.0
Thread model: posix
InstalledDir: /opt/homebrew/Cellar/llvm/22.1.8/bin
Configuration file: /opt/homebrew/Cellar/llvm/22.1.8/etc/clang/arm64-apple-darwin27.cfg
findings: C and AOT each call the same separately compiled, noinline, non-LTO CLOCK_MONOTONIC_RAW helper immediately around the kernel. No system I/O, array initialization, checksum, or output function is in the optimized kernel envelope.

Every serial kernel has its result load/arithmetic/store loop between start and stop in optimized LLVM and AArch64 assembly. Prime overflow-error paths remain reachable; output/checksum safety checks outside the envelope are not counted as kernel cost.

Fresh-parallel envelopes contain the external parallel-for-each call, including thread creation/join and callback overhead inside that runtime. Static caller IR does not measure actual successful thread starts or inspect JIT-generated machine code.

Clang duplicates the two-iteration outer loop in tiny C serial and all C parallel entries, producing two lexical start/stop pairs; the Aevix entry retains one lexical pair executed twice. Both source protocols still perform one warmup followed by one sampled kernel.

All four actual kernels are scalar in the prepared O2 IR and assembly. The whole entry function has SIMD for input initialization and SIMD-shaped output descriptors outside the clock envelope; those are not kernel SIMD.

LCG kernel overflow checks and fixed-array bound checks disappear under matching Clang O2 with proof optimization explicitly off. Prime retains three unsigned overflow intrinsics/trap paths in Aevix; C uses unsigned wrap semantics and has no corresponding traps.

C and AOT use explicit arm64-apple-macosx and produce the same arm64-apple-macosx28.0.0 triple. C IR records apple-m1; Aevix raw-to-final IR has no explicit CPU attribute, and the same Clang target defaults to apple-m1. JIT detects host CPU; its supported command has no equal-target override.

Clock declarations have no readnone/readonly memory effect. This opaque external call plus runtime seed input and post-clock observable stores are evidence against moving the inspected loop outside the clocks; this is a static envelope check, not an equal-performance guarantee.
limits: Optimized LLVM and matching Clang assembly were prepared before this audit; no binary was rebuilt or run here.
Lexical assembly excerpts do not alone include cold out-of-line trap targets; CFG-reachable LLVM regions include their trap calls.
For parallel mode the worker body is separately recorded because an external runtime invokes it indirectly.
AOT linked-binary disassembly and JIT generated-code capture are separate evidence; this report does not claim either from standalone .s files.
